hook.line: Official Spanish loves to say "the building whose owners live in Miami" in one breath. The little word for "whose" is *cuyo*, and you will meet it in notices, contracts and news reports.
hook.es: El edificio, cuyos dueños viven en Miami, será vendido.
hook.en: The building, whose owners live in Miami, will be sold.

examples.es: El edificio, cuyos dueños viven en Miami, será vendido.
examples.en: The building, whose owners live in Miami, will be sold.

examples.es: Conozco a una mujer cuyo hijo trabaja en la Alcaldía.
examples.en: I know a woman whose son works at City Hall.

examples.es: Es una tienda cuyas empleadas son todas mujeres.
examples.en: It's a shop whose employees are all women.

examples.es: Don Hernando, cuyo carro tiene treinta años, nunca llega tarde.
examples.en: Don Hernando, whose car is thirty years old, is never late.

examples.es: Altamira, cuyo proyecto afecta a toda la cuadra, quiere comprar el café.
examples.en: Altamira, whose project affects the whole block, wants to buy the café.

examples.es: Tengo un amigo cuyos padres viven en Toronto.
examples.en: I have a friend whose parents live in Toronto.

rule:
*Cuyo* means "whose". It joins two ideas: *una mujer* + *su hijo trabaja en la Alcaldía* becomes *una mujer cuyo hijo trabaja en la Alcaldía*.

Two things differ from English:
*Cuyo* agrees with the thing owned, not the owner: *cuyo hijo*, *cuyos hijos*, *cuya casa*, *cuyas casas*.
No *el*, *la* or *su* follows it: *cuyos dueños*, never *cuyos los dueños*.

It belongs to writing and formal speech. In chat people use two sentences: *Conozco a una mujer. Su hijo trabaja en la Alcaldía.* You need *cuyo* to read the formal kind.
smallPrint: Teachers call *cuyo* a possessive relative. It is an adjective, which is why it agrees like one.

readAndPick.es: Conozco al señor cuyas hijas viven en Cali.
options: the man whose daughter lives in Cali
the man whose daughters live in Cali
the man who lives with his daughters in Cali

readAndPick.es: Es una empresa cuyo dueño vive en Miami.
options: a company whose owner lives in Miami
a company whose owners live in Miami
a company that lives in Miami

readAndPick.es: Hablé con la vecina cuya casa está en venta.
options: I spoke with the neighbour whose house is for sale.
I spoke with the neighbour whose houses are for sale.
I spoke with the neighbours whose house is for sale.

readAndPick.es: Es un barrio cuyos edificios son muy viejos.
options: a neighbourhood whose building is very old
a neighbourhood whose buildings are very old
a neighbourhood with a very old owner

readAndPick.es: Vale, cuyo pan de bono es famoso, abre a las seis.
options: Vale, whose cheese bread is famous, opens at six.
Vale, whose cheese breads are famous, open at six.
Vale, who is famous for bread, opens at six.

readAndPick.es: Es una oficina cuyas reglas son claras.
options: an office whose rule is clear
an office whose rules are clear
an office that makes clear rules

readAndPick.es: Mariana escribe sobre un hombre cuyo nombre nadie recuerda.
options: Mariana writes about a man whose names nobody remembers.
Mariana writes about men whose name nobody remembers.
Mariana writes about a man whose name nobody remembers.

readAndPick.es: Conozco a unos socios cuyo voto fue decisivo.
options: I know some members whose vote was decisive.
I know some members whose votes were decisive.
I know a member whose vote was decisive.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *cuyos* or *cuyo* and type the whole sentence: *El edificio, ___ dueños viven en Miami, será vendido.*
yourTurn.answer: El edificio, cuyos dueños viven en Miami, será vendido.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *cuya* or *cuyas* and type the whole sentence: *Es una tienda ___ empleadas son todas mujeres.*
yourTurn.answer: Es una tienda cuyas empleadas son todas mujeres.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I know a woman whose son works at City Hall.
yourTurn.answer: Conozco a una mujer cuyo hijo trabaja en la Alcaldía.
accept: Yo conozco a una mujer cuyo hijo trabaja en la Alcaldía.
yourTurn.why: *Hijo* is one boy, so *cuyo*, even though the owner is a woman.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I have a friend whose parents live in Toronto.
yourTurn.answer: Tengo un amigo cuyos padres viven en Toronto.
accept: Yo tengo un amigo cuyos padres viven en Toronto.

yourTurn.prompt: Join the two sentences with *cuyo*: *Conozco a un señor. Su carro tiene treinta años.* Say: I know a man whose car is thirty years old.
yourTurn.answer: Conozco a un señor cuyo carro tiene treinta años.
accept: Yo conozco a un señor cuyo carro tiene treinta años.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: It's a neighbourhood whose buildings are very old.
yourTurn.answer: Es un barrio cuyos edificios son muy viejos.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Altamira, whose project affects the whole block, wants to buy the café.
yourTurn.answer: Altamira, cuyo proyecto afecta a toda la cuadra, quiere comprar el café.
yourTurn.why: *Proyecto* is one masculine thing, so *cuyo*, set off by commas.

pitfalls.wrong: Conozco a una mujer que su hijo trabaja en la Alcaldía.
pitfalls.right: Conozco a una mujer cuyo hijo trabaja en la Alcaldía.
pitfalls.why: Almost. People do say *que su* in chat, but in writing *cuyo* does that job.

pitfalls.wrong: Conozco a una mujer cuya hijos trabajan aquí.
pitfalls.right: Conozco a una mujer cuyos hijos trabajan aquí.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Cuyo* agrees with what is owned (*hijos*), not with the owner (*mujer*).

pitfalls.wrong: El edificio, cuyos los dueños viven en Miami, será vendido.
pitfalls.right: El edificio, cuyos dueños viven en Miami, será vendido.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Cuyo* already means "whose the", so no *los* follows it.
Almost. *Cuyo* never asks a question; for "whose is it?" use *de quién*.

personal: Describe someone you know with *cuyo*: a friend whose job, house or family you can say something true about.
